limitations: The closure checker is my own code written from prose; a defect in it is mine, not the design's.
Schema validation, helper predicates, full retained closure and future host enforcement are four different things and are kept apart; everything here is the first three.
Every OS, compiler, cryptographic, SQLite, filesystem, custody, revocation and confinement observation is a synthetic TCB assumption, never native enforcement proof.
The positive Runs use synthetic trusted provider output; they qualify no provider, compiler, grammar, normalizer or platform.
The trust-time (S4/S4.5), root-chain (S5), revocation (S6), lease (S7), migration (S9) and installation-journal (S9.2) state machines were read but not reconstructed; no vector depends on them.
The fold used for the libSelection join does not discriminate U+0130, Final_Sigma or U+00DF because every current lib name is ASCII, where the three candidate operations coincide.

This pass corrected TWO real defects in my own validator that the original pass did not catch. The corrected checker is still my own code written from prose; the same class of omission may remain elsewhere.

My measured affected set differs from root's stated count: SIX original graphs are refused by the corrected checker, not five, because RUN-RS-NO-OWNERSHIP-DISCLOSED also carries unordered finding.evidenceRefs.
Root's diagnostic copies were neither supplied to me nor used as an oracle; every conclusion here is my own measurement over the unchanged kit.

retractedFindings.originalTitle: The mandated per-requirement cause carrier cannot express 11 of 16 producible outcomes
retractedFindings.whyRetracted: the finding rested on an equation the kit never states - `unmetPreconditions[].code == the deficiency token`. workflows-and-surfaces S6 requires that two different causes be two different REMEDIES, and DomainDetail carries a required `remedy` BoundedText.

repairEvidenceRunUnavailableAssessed.boundConditionInTheKit: workflows-and-surfaces.md S6: the evidence Run 'whose availability is retained and whose sealed assurance is replayable (else the plan is not applicable with REPAIR.EVIDENCE_RUN_UNAVAILABLE)'
repairEvidenceRunUnavailableAssessed.conclusion: Not applicable - and NOT needed, because the outcome's named carrier is EvidenceRequirement.deficiency, not an unmetPreconditions code.
repairEvidenceRunUnavailableAssessed.why: It names retained AVAILABILITY and replayable sealed ASSURANCE of the evidence Run. An unsatisfied evidence requirement is a different condition: the Run is available and replayable, and the evidence it carries is insufficient at the demanded rung. Borrowing it would misname the condition, which is the same objection this review raised against borrowing REPAIR.CLOSED_WORLD_NOT_ESTABLISHED.

discriminatingControl.note: collapsing both causes onto one remedy string is what the purpose clause forbids; the two descriptors then differ only in evidenceRequirements, and the REMEDY no longer distinguishes them

expressibleVersusAuthorized.conclusion: An expressible, schema-admitted RepairPlanV1 carrying an unsatisfied requirement is a DISCLOSURE. It is not an authorized repair: applicable is false, and any edit to the descriptor mints a different repairPlanId that no authorization names.
